name: The Beekman
insider_take: This 1881 architectural marvel transforms a historic publishing house into Manhattan's most Instagram-worthy atrium hotel.
whats_special: The Beekman's stunning 9-story Victorian atrium features original cast-iron railings and a breathtaking pyramidal skylight. Celebrity chefs Tom Colicchio and Keith McNally operate the hotel's acclaimed restaurants, while the building once housed the offices of *Beekman's Mercantile* and later served as the headquarters for Nassau Street's newspaper row.
pro_tip: Book a room overlooking the atrium for the ultimate "wow factor" – the natural light filtering through the skylight creates magical photo opportunities throughout the day.
dont_miss: Temple Court restaurant's raw bar and Keith McNally's Augustine brasserie. Step outside to explore Stone Street's cobblestone dining scene and you're just a 3-minute walk to the South Street Seaport's waterfront views and historic ships.
pros: Historic landmark building with stunning Victorian architecture and soaring atrium
Prime Financial District location near Brooklyn Bridge and South Street Seaport
Acclaimed Temple Court restaurant and rooftop bar with city views
Luxurious rooms with high ceilings and elegant period-inspired design
cons: Premium pricing typical of luxury NYC hotels
Historic building constraints may limit some modern amenities
